g3ela-27-1-teach-morph: [curious] Two little word parts, one big job. The parts at the front of these words both mean not. Inactive means not active. Impolite means not polite. Here's the trick: im comes before words that start with m or p, like polite. Read the four words, and tap See if you were right. Then type the base word hiding in each one.
g3ela-27-1-teach-vocab: Be a word detective with me. Sternly. Here's the sentence. Aslan a man, said Mr. Beaver sternly. One, read the sentence: he sounds serious, maybe a little cross. Two, look for word parts: stern, plus l y. Three, check it. Sternly means in a strict, serious way. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.
g3ela-27-1-teach-gram: [warmly] Most verbs add e d for the past. Walk, walked. But some verbs break the rule. Listen. Mr. Beaver catched a fish. Catched? No! It's caught. Verbs like that are called irregular. You learn them one at a time. Read The Rule box, and tap Now check your thinking. Then find the four verbs that should not end in e d.
g3ela-27-1-teach-spell: Some long words are a short word with an extra part on the front. Replay. Cover the front part. What's left? Play! That front part means again, so replay means play again. Peel off the front, read the base word, then put it back. Tap Now name the pattern. Then sort the words.
g3ela-27-2-teach-morph: Watch one match first. Incomplete. Find the word part at the front. It means not. What's left? Complete. So incomplete means not complete, like a puzzle with a missing piece. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.
g3ela-27-2-teach-vocab: Here's a cozy word from Chapter 7. Snug. Lucy thinks the Beavers have a very snug little home. Warm, cozy and safe! Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four.
g3ela-27-2-teach-gram: Spot the wrong verb. The children drinked hot tea. Drinked? That's not a word! The past of drink is drank. The children drank hot tea. Check the verb in each of the four sentences, and tap Now check your thinking. Then fix the paragraph.
g3ela-27-2-teach-spell: Prefix hunt! Here's my sentence. Mom will preview the movie, then rewind the best part. Preview. Pre, plus view. Rewind. Re, plus wind. Two prefix words! Read the rule. Then tap every word built from a prefix and a base word.
g3ela-27-2-teach-rwm: [warmly] Let's try all three parts with a different sentence from Chapter 8. He is our brother after all, even if he is rather a little beast. Part one, read like a reader. Peter is cross with Edmund, but he still wants to find him. Part two, read like a writer. After all, and even if, let Peter hold two feelings in one sentence. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: She is my best friend after all, even if she eats the last cookie. Now it's your turn with the sentence about the whiskered face. Write one sentence in each box.
g3ela-27-3-teach-morph: Snap the parts together. Im. Mature. Immature! Immature means not grown up yet, like a puppy chewing your shoes. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.
g3ela-27-3-teach-vocab: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Here's my sentence. The children ate dinner in the Beavers' blank little house. Treachery? Hmm, no. Snug? Yes! Now pick the word that fits each sentence.
g3ela-27-3-teach-gram: Let's fix a sentence the way the editor did. Mr. Beaver keeped a hole open in the ice. Keeped? The past of keep is kept. Mr. Beaver kept a hole open in the ice. Read the before and after, and tap Check yourself. Then fix the sentence, and list three more verbs like these.
g3ela-27-3-teach-spell: Proofreader time! Here's a word with a mistake. Unsaif. Peel off the front part. What's left should be safe: s, a, f, e. The base word never changes, so it's unsafe. Read the rule. Then tap the words you think are spelled wrong.
g3ela-27-4-teach-morph: Quick! What do these two word parts mean? Not! Here's a word that's not on the dice. Indirect. A path that's not direct winds around, like Edmund's walk through the snow. Now tap Roll the Dice. Say what each word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six.
g3ela-27-4-teach-vocab: Here's how I'd use a word about the story. Gloating. Edmund stood gloating over the stone lion, because he thought the Witch had won. One word, one moment. Now choose one of your words and write your own sentence about Chapters 7 to 9.
g3ela-27-4-teach-gram: Three passes, like an editor. mrs beaver maked a marmalade roll and they ate it all. Pass one, capitals: Mrs. and Beaver. Pass two, verbs: maked becomes made. Pass three, a comma before and. Now do your passes, and tap every word that needs fixing.
g3ela-27-4-teach-spell: Here's my roll. Misbehave. Peel off the front part. The base word is behave. The front part means badly, so misbehave means behave badly. Tap Roll the dice, name the prefix and the base word, and tap Check my answer.
